cut.title: Returned-item slip, form P-9
cut.why: scored 6, under 7: A plain, specific piece of ordinary postal life in an empty year; it leaves the Ring Road and Block 4 open rather than explaining them.

cut.title: Stores receipt for the second pressing of Die Signalgruppe
cut.why: cut by the reader: It mostly writes up a fact the figures page already states, and the Section F link ties it to FORECAST too tidily, then spells out the connection.

cut.title: Ubikistan Games poster with paste-over slip
cut.why: cut by the reader: It turns the sport page's joke about the pool into a literal poster and explains it, and its contradiction with the 1977 programme is too neat to be worth keeping.

cut.title: Routing slip for a press cutting on Grey Radio
cut.why: cut by the reader: It only decorates the single line 'The company kept the review', and four ticked boxes with a 'Keep' from A. add nothing that line did not already say.

cut.title: Delivery round card, plain round 1
cut.why: uses a word the archive did not allow then (pump); the filter has since been corrected

cut.title: Embassy appointments screen, last day, printed
cut.why: scored 6, under 7: Gives the thin 2020 Virtual Continuity a working object with AIXBT doing his job, and leaves open whether this was the server that came back on in 2026; the provenance line is simplified.

cut.title: Store tally card, Die Signalgruppe second pressing
cut.why: cut by the reader: It mostly restates the Signalgruppe fact already on file, and the blank 1985 row is a symbolic nod to the Missing Year, which was a gap in the digital copy, not on paper.

filed.gap: UNT has no records in the Network era; thin year 2011
filed.test: Changes what we know about UBIK
filed.reader: 8/10, UBIK reduced to a voice with no picture matches his withdrawal from his own images in the Network era, and it gives UNT its first record of that era.

filed.gap: Thin year 1980, no records; Die Signalgruppe and the second pressing the Ministry bought and never distributed
filed.reader: 7/10, A small, dry object that contradicts the Figures page ('never distributed') and says so in its text, with a loose thread to Station 6 that it leaves open.

cut.title: Application for a change of holder class, returned
cut.why: another find from the same decade scored higher, or enough were kept

cut.title: Carrier's round book, round 4, the Ring Estate
cut.why: cut by the reader: The postal texture is good, but the parcel to THE FOUNDER signed for by 'A.' is a wink at the reader, and the Ring Estate and the Relay Line are places the archive has never named and this record does not establish.

filed.gap: Thin year 1967 (no records); the State Post in its first full year
filed.test: Shows a part of ordinary life not shown yet
filed.reader: 7/10, A plain, messy piece of ordinary life in an empty year, with AIXBT's initial where his 1966 office says it should be and an unexplained Plot 0 that stays unexplained.

filed.gap: Person on file with no records: M-Keys (active 1994–2004); thin year 2002
filed.reader: 7/10, Contradicts the M-Keys entry in Figures in a useful way: the key proves itself but no person turns up, so the gap stays open; the last paragraph is rewritten to state the contradiction plainly.

cut.title: Embassy closure checklist, printed from the work-order screen
cut.why: another find from the same decade scored higher, or enough were kept

cut.title: Import permit, nitrogen fertiliser for the Glasshouses, returned
cut.why: cut by the reader: The Glasshouses permit would be good on its own, but the Section F routing tab is a hook bolted on to reach Station 6, and the body explains it ('Section F was the FORECAST section') instead of leaving it alone.

filed.gap: People on file with no records: The Pale Index and the F-Series tape bought at auction in 1988
filed.reader: 7/10, It gives The Pale Index's tape a paper trail, states its contradiction with the 1987 sealing order, and leaves the forecast-timings question open behind a struck-through pencil line.

cut.title: Public Works pledge card, returned, Ring Estate plot 22
cut.why: scored 6, under 7: It shows ordinary life answering the 1969 campaign, the dry refusal reads like a real ministry, and the plot 21/22 link to the round card is earned without being explained; I only tightened the provenance sentence.

cut.title: Annual confirmation of registration, Network Citizen No. 1, question 3 unanswered
cut.why: scored 6, under 7: It fills the empty year 2000 with a plausible form and leaves the agent question disputed, but the 'A.R.' reading of the initials is a wink at Anton Rey, so it has been removed.

cut.title: Key board, Embassy porter's lodge, hook 15 empty
cut.why: cut by the reader: A server key retained by AIXBT is too neat an answer to how the old embassy server came back on in 2026, and the empty SRV hook is symbolism rather than a mess an archive would actually hold.

filed.gap: Pavel Oric, person on file with no records
filed.reader: 7/10, Gives Pavel Oric his first record, and its contradiction with Figures of the Republic (premature on the carbon that was sent, impractical only in the file note) is small, plain and stated.

filed.gap: Thin year 2007 (no records); the Sporting Committee absent from the Product Age
filed.reader: 7/10, Brings the Sporting Committee into the Product Age and shows FIELD in ordinary use, and rider 31, logged by the sensors but not seen by the marshal, stays unexplained.

cut.title: Reply coupons, Public Works campaign, bundle of eleven
cut.why: scored 6, under 7: Ordinary life in a thin year, with good mess (the bench crossed out because the square stays empty); the last sentence spells out an echo of the 1967 round card that readers can find through the related records.

cut.title: Embassy keys returned on closure, with receipt
cut.why: cut by the reader: The struck-out SERVER tag and the retained key are a neat setup for the 2026 reopening that explains the server's return, and the closing line points out the connection while claiming not to make it.

filed.gap: 1969, a thin year; the first Public Works campaign has only its poster
filed.test: Shows a part of ordinary life not shown yet
filed.reader: 7/10, A plain, messy piece of ordinary life from a thin year: the campaign called for builders, no office could take the offer, and cards 0001 to 0186 are missing, all stated without explanation.

filed.gap: The Border Service in the Emergence, with no records; 2020, Virtual Continuity, a thin year
filed.reader: 7/10, It is the first record of the 2020 Embassy closure from inside the state: a dry inventory with a missing DUPLICATE stamp and an unsigned note on the server room, which leads to the 2026 reopening without settling anything.

cut.title: Register screen, Network Citizen 0001, annual confirmation
cut.why: cut by the reader: The confirmation arriving one second after midnight all but answers whether the First Network Citizen was an agent, which is a deliberately disputed gap, and the closing paragraph explains what the printout means.

cut.title: Facility request, training pool, Ubikistan Games 2012, refused
cut.why: cut by the reader: It only acts out a line the Sport lore already gives (no swimming, the only pool belongs to the space programme), and it ends by explaining its own point.

filed.gap: Thin year 1980; UNT has few Republic-era objects; the FORECAST thread seen from outside Station 6
filed.test: Shows a part of ordinary life not shown yet
filed.reader: 7/10, An ordinary broadcast object from a thin year that lets an unnamed Directorate quietly overrule the weather, and leaves the link to FORECAST unproven and unexplained.

filed.gap: Thin year 2022; the Register of Synthetic Persons has no records in the Emergence; the first agent citizen's name
filed.reader: 7/10, A dry register printout from a thin year that plainly states a real contradiction with the canonical date and leaves the passport question open.

cut.title: Application to register a performing group, The Pale Index, with correction slip
cut.why: cut by the reader: Mostly restates the 1988 disposal list and the Figures entry with invented names attached, and the closing line about no track is the find winking at its own joke.

cut.title: Returned envelope, Register notice to Network Citizen No. 1, unopened
cut.why: cut by the reader: The contradiction is a calendar quibble that the body explains away, and 'leave it with the machines' leans toward settling whether the first Network Citizen was an agent, which is a deliberate open question.

filed.gap: 2000 has no records; the Ministry for Machine Affairs has one record in the whole Archive
filed.test: It shows ordinary life not shown yet: the counters of the Republic on the first working day of 2000
filed.reader: 8/10, It shows ordinary counter life in an empty year and echoes the Missing Year with a clock set to 1986 without explaining it; the places and the institution are right.

filed.gap: The Treaty of the Open Centre (1972) has no object in the Archive; UNT has nothing between 1970 and 1980
filed.test: It moves the history on: the first object from the signing of the Treaty at Sector 03
filed.reader: 7/10, It is the first object from the Treaty signing, and it leaves the event as empty as the ring: no picture, no date, and a reel that may not be the right one.

cut.title: Reading room request slip, IAC drawings, Cognitive Array, revision C
cut.why: another find from the same decade scored higher, or enough were kept

cut.title: Form R-3, registration of a recorded work, The Pale Index
cut.why: cut by the reader: It mostly restates what Figures of the Republic and the 1988 disposal list already say, and track titles like "Cooling Line B" and "Ring 2" point too neatly at Station 6.

filed.gap: people_on_file: The Pale Index, no records
filed.test: Shows a part of ordinary life not shown yet: the NICC night shift off duty
filed.reader: 8/10, It gives The Pale Index its first record as a photograph, ties the band to lot 9 in a dry way, and the half-read reel number 41 hints that the reels were never erased without saying so.

filed.gap: institutions_by_era: Ministry of Culture, no records in the Technology State
filed.reader: 7/10, An object that gives the Ministry of Culture a record in the Technology State, with a plainly stated contradiction on the date of the Advanced Systems Group and on who designed the earpiece; one sentence explaining the point is cut.

cut.title: Weather, UNT NEWS 1, frame from a telerecording
cut.why: scored 6, under 7: A film still that shows the UNT weather desk for the first time, puts the Weather Ridge and the Glasshouses on a map, and leaves the M.T. question open without answering it.

cut.title: Postman on round 4, the Ring Estate
cut.why: cut by the reader: A pleasant photograph, but it mostly illustrates the round card of the same month and round, and the plot 10 link is a neat tie-in rather than something new.

cut.title: Staff photograph, UBIK Systems, the lawn of the Quiet Pavilions
cut.why: cut by the reader: The blurred ivory figure at the edge and the unnamed number 143 are a familiar ghost trope that is too neat a symbol, and a group of 140 faces will be hard to make look right.

cut.title: Self-service postage label, Relay Line kiosk 2, paid by UBIK ID, on a returned envelope
cut.why: cut by the reader: It reuses Plot 0 from another unreviewed MOTH find to make a tidy running echo, explains its own significance ("the first item with no picture"), and is mostly paperwork.

filed.gap: Thin year 1970 (one record); UNT has no photograph of its own weather service
filed.test: Shows an institution for the first time: UNT's weather observing post on the Weather Ridge
filed.reader: 7/10, A real photograph that shows UNT's weather post for the first time and fills a thin year; the rubbed-out 'use with frost' note points too neatly at the 1980 script, so it is removed.

filed.gap: Thin year 2012; the Ring Estate and ordinary home life in the Network era
filed.test: Shows a part of ordinary life not shown yet: a living room on the Ring Estate while UBIK is on the television
filed.reader: 7/10, Ordinary life on the Ring Estate, with UBIK only as a portrait above an empty podium that nobody watches, which fits his withdrawal; the plot 17 dog joke explains itself and is cut.

cut.title: KNOW YOUR NOTE, counterfeit warning, Series A
cut.why: no picture passed the look-over; MOTH files pictures, not text alone

cut.title: Visitor passes, Grey Radio tour, one not issued
cut.why: cut by the reader: Mostly decorates the Grey Radio tour that is already on file, and it cites a published account of the visit even though the archive says the rest of the review is not held.

filed.gap: Ubikistan National Television has no records in the Product Age (1996–2008); thin year 2005
filed.test: Shows a part of ordinary life not shown yet
filed.reader: 7/10, A photograph of ordinary work in UNT's empty Product Age years that moves the M.T. thread on, puts a woman where the 1970 print has a man and leaves the question open, with the grey box arriving before FIELD left unnamed.

cut.title: Store level board, Heat Wells pump house 3, removed on fitting of a level sensor
cut.why: no picture passed the look-over; MOTH files pictures, not text alone

cut.title: Ring Estate, block 2 under construction, plots 15 to 18
cut.why: cut by the reader: The dog tied to the unmarked stake between 16 and 18 is there only to explain the round card's note on plot 17 and to link it to the 2012 flat, so the photograph is a neat answer when it should be a record of ordinary life.

cut.title: Imperforate proof block, Assembly of the Republic, 20 U, date tablet blank
cut.why: cut by the reader: An empty chamber with a blank date box is a symbol of the Silent Congress, not evidence of it, and it only decorates an event the timeline and the stamp list already cover.
